title: Agent2Agent (A2A) Protocol
hook: A2A is an open standard for agents from different vendors to discover and delegate to each other — the agent-to-agent complement to MCP's agent-to-tool layer.
key_points: Open protocol announced by Google in April 2025 with 50+ founding partners.
Lets agents built on different frameworks discover each other and coordinate tasks.
Uses HTTP, Server-Sent Events, and JSON-RPC, with 'Agent Cards' advertising capabilities.
Donated to the Linux Foundation in June 2025 for vendor-neutral governance.
content_html: The Agent2Agent (A2A) protocol, announced by Google in April 2025, is an open standard for interoperability between AI agents. Where the Model Context Protocol (MCP) connects an agent to tools and data, A2A connects agents to each other: it lets agents built by different vendors, on different frameworks, discover one another's capabilities and delegate work.
extra_html:
How it works

A2A uses ordinary web plumbing — HTTP, Server-Sent Events for streaming, and JSON-RPC for calls — so it is straightforward to adopt. Each agent publishes an "Agent Card" describing what it can do, which other agents read to decide how to route a task. The launch included more than 50 technology and consulting partners, and in June 2025 Google donated A2A to the Linux Foundation, putting it under neutral governance with backers including AWS, Microsoft, Salesforce, and SAP.

Why it matters

As organizations deploy many specialized agents, those agents need a common language to cooperate without bespoke integrations for every pair. A2A and MCP are complementary halves of an emerging agent stack — one for talking to tools, the other for talking to agents — and moving A2A to the Linux Foundation signaled an intent to make it a shared standard rather than one company's API.
